subject: Linguistics
title: Arbitrariness of the Sign
description: A quick, practical guide to Arbitrariness of the Sign.

hook.text: A dog is called 'dog' in English, 'chien' in French, and 'inu' in Japanese.

buildup.text: There's no natural link between the sound and the animal—the connection is arbitrary.

discovery.text: Saussure called this the arbitrariness of the sign: words are social contracts, not labels.

twist.text: Onomatopoeia seems to break the rule, but even 'cock-a-doodle-doo' differs across languages.

climax.text: This arbitrariness is powerful—it lets language expand to name anything imaginable.

punchline.text: Words mean what we agree they mean.

quiz.question: Who introduced the concept of the arbitrariness of the sign?
